topics.notes_md: Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) is a programming paradigm based on the concept of "objects", which can contain data, in the form of fields (often known as attributes), and code, in the form of procedures (often known as methods). A central feature of OOP is the concept of data encapsulation, which hides the internal representation of an object from the outside world and only exposes a set of methods for interacting with the object. Other core principles include inheritance (allowing new classes to inherit properties and behaviors from existing classes), and polymorphism (allowing objects of different classes to be treated as objects of a common type). OOP promotes code reusability, maintainability, and scalability.

Describe the benefits of using OOP.

topics.notes_md: C++ is a general-purpose programming language. It is regarded as a middle-level language, as it comprises a combination of both high-level and low-level language features. It was developed by Bjarne Stroustrup starting in 1979 at Bell Labs as an enhancement to the C language. C++ is widely used for developing operating systems, game development, device drivers, servers, performance-critical applications, and entertainment software. C++ supports both procedural and object-oriented programming paradigms, providing flexibility in designing software solutions.  It also supports features like operator overloading and exception handling. C++ code is typically compiled into machine code for direct execution by the computer's processor.

topics.notes_md: A constructor is a special member function that is automatically called when an object is created. It is used to initialize the object's attributes. A destructor is a special member function that is automatically called when an object is destroyed. It is used to release any resources held by the object. Constructors have the same name as the class. Destructors have the same name as the class, preceded by a tilde (`~`).  Constructors can be overloaded to provide different initialization options. Destructors have no parameters.

topics.topic_title: Access Modifiers: Public, Private, and Protected
topics.notes_md: Access modifiers control the visibility of class members. `public` members are accessible from anywhere. `private` members are only accessible from within the class. `protected` members are accessible from within the class and its derived classes. Encapsulation is achieved by making data members private and providing public member functions to access and modify them. This protects the data from direct manipulation and ensures data integrity. It allows for controlled access and modification of the object's internal state.

topics.notes_md: Inheritance allows a class (derived class) to inherit properties and behaviors from another class (base class). Single inheritance involves inheriting from one base class. Multiple inheritance involves inheriting from multiple base classes. Hierarchical inheritance involves multiple derived classes inheriting from a single base class. Inheritance promotes code reusability and reduces code duplication. It also allows for creating a hierarchy of classes with specialized functionalities. The syntax for inheritance is `class DerivedClass : access_modifier BaseClass`. `access_modifier` can be `public`, `private`, or `protected`.

topics.notes_md: Polymorphism means "many forms". It allows objects of different classes to be treated as objects of a common type. Function overloading allows multiple functions with the same name but different parameters. Function overriding allows a derived class to provide a specific implementation of a function that is already defined in its base class. Overriding is achieved using the `virtual` keyword in the base class and the `override` keyword in the derived class. Polymorphism enhances code flexibility and extensibility.

topics.notes_md: A virtual function is a member function that is declared with the `virtual` keyword. It allows derived classes to override the function's behavior. An abstract class is a class that contains at least one pure virtual function (a virtual function that is declared with `= 0`). Abstract classes cannot be instantiated. They serve as base classes for other classes. Abstract classes define a common interface for their derived classes. Virtual functions enable runtime polymorphism.

topics.notes_md: Templates allow you to write generic code that can work with different data types. Function templates define a generic function that can operate on different types. Class templates define a generic class that can hold different types. Templates promote code reusability and reduce code duplication. Template parameters are specified using the `template` keyword. Template instantiation occurs when the compiler generates code for a specific data type.

topics.notes_md: Exception handling is a mechanism for handling runtime errors. `try` block encloses code that might throw an exception. `catch` block handles exceptions that are thrown within the `try` block. `throw` keyword is used to throw an exception. Exception handling improves code robustness and prevents program crashes. Standard exception classes are defined in the `<stdexcept>` header. Custom exception classes can be defined to handle specific errors.
